instantiated_cells.justification: Activity reporting duties in this chapter are imposed on registrants (lobbyists) monthly (§305.007(a)), with only a registrant’s optional modified method requiring an annual filing (§305.0063(c)), not a principal spending report.

The periodic activity report is required of each 'registrant' (lobbyist) (§305.006(a)) and filed monthly (§305.007(a)), but the statute does not impose periodic spending reports on principals/employers.

All periodic reporting mechanisms described (registration, amended registration, activity reports, termination notice) apply to registrants and do not create any alternative principal reporting frequency.

The statute requires registrants to file monthly activity reports (§305.007(a)) and provides an annual report for certain registrants (§305.0063(c)), but does not require quarterly reports by principals.
No provision requires principals to file semi-annual spending reports; the only periodic reports required are registrant (lobbyist) reports.

The reporting schedule in this chapter is monthly for registrants (§305.007(a)), with a registrant annual report option (§305.0063(c)), and contains no tri-annual/legislative-calendar reporting for principals.
Because the statute does not require principals to file periodic spending reports at all, there is no 'other' reporting frequency to specify for principals.

Registration disclosures concern registrants listing each person who reimburses/retains/employs the registrant (§305.005(f)(3)), but the statute does not require principals to file reports disclosing their business nature.
Compensation or reimbursement amounts are reported by the registrant in the registration statement (§305.005(f)(6)), not by principals through a principal spending report.

The statute requires registrants to disclose subject matters and expenditures and to list categories of subject matters communicated about (§305.006(d)), but does not require principals to disclose contacts.
Issue/subject-matter disclosure is required in a registrant’s registration and activity reports (§305.005(f)(4); §305.006(d)), not in any principal-filed spending report.

Gifts, entertainment, transportation, and lodging expenditures are components of the registrant’s activities report (§305.006(b)), and the chapter does not impose analogous cost reporting duties on principals.

The chapter requires registrants to report certain expenditures including mass media communications (§305.006(b), (c)), but it does not require principals to report indirect (non-compensation) lobbying costs.

Business address and occupation reporting applies to persons employed or retained by the registrant as assistants (§305.005(f)(5)(A)), not to principals disclosing address/phone of contracted lobbyists in a principal spending report.

The registration statement requires the registrant to list each person who employs/reimburses the registrant (§305.005(f)(3)), but the statute does not require principals to list all lobbyists representing them via principal reports.
Major contributor disclosure is required only on certain registrant registration forms when lobbying is on behalf of a group/organization (§305.005(h)(4)), not as a principal reporting obligation.

While principals’ names and addresses may appear because registrants must disclose the 'full name and address' of each person who employs/reimburses them (§305.005(f)(3)), the statute does not impose a duty on principals themselves to disclose their address/phone via a principal spending report.

Specific administrative docket numbers may be required in registrant registration subject-matter disclosures (§305.005(f)(4)), but there is no principal spending report requiring bill numbers/IDs from principals.

The chapter requires registrants to report certain total expenditures for lobbying communications in defined categories (§305.006(b)), but it does not require principals to report total lobbying expenditures (in-house plus consulting).

Although registrants must disclose compensation/reimbursement paid by each client (§305.005(f)(6)), the statute creates no employer/principal spending report requiring employers to report salary/fees paid to lobbyists.

Itemized details (e.g., naming the official, place/date, gift description) are required in certain circumstances on a registrant’s report (§305.0061), but principals are not required to file itemized spending reports.
Listing the persons who determine policy in a group/organization is a registrant registration requirement (§305.005(h)(2)), not a principal’s periodic spending-report obligation.
The chapter regulates lobbyist (registrant) registration and activity reporting and does not require companies/principals to file a report listing the lobbyists they employ.
